title: Contract formation versus selection of terms
shortTitle: Contract formation versus selection of terms
summary: Contract formation asks whether an agreement has become a contract. Term identification asks what obligations that contract contains. The two questions can require different evidence and rules.
notes:
Section 2-207 makes the distinction especially visible: a contract may exist despite nonmatching forms, while the disputed clause is excluded. Later interpretation materials distinguish identifying an agreement from deciding what a writing means or whether other agreed terms supplement it. Always identify which question the court is deciding before treating its conclusion as a general rule of assent or validity.

Under § 2-207(1), an expression of acceptance can form a contract despite differences; subsection (2) then addresses additional terms. If the writings fail but the parties perform, subsection (3) supplies a different formation-and-terms route. Hill and Klocek disagree at an earlier stage about whether the transaction was already formed when the terms arrived. The classification of the sequence often determines the next test.
